newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Don shares bounce off recent lows.
newsitem.headline: Don shares bounce off recent lows.

text.p: Shares in The Don Group, a South African apartment and restaurant group, staged a mild recovery on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Thursday after a downward trend of some eight months, dealers said.
"The share price has come down enormously in the past few months," a dealer said.
"It looks like it is a bit of a bounce because it got smacked so hard."
Dealers said the hotels sector in which the Don Group competes had seen fierce competition recently.
"Conditions in that industry don't look good. One hears of rooms in good hotels being offered for as little as 125 rand a night," one dealer said.

By 1035 GMT Don shares were up nearly eight percent or 12 cents at 166 rand, rising off a year low of 154 cents touched on Wednesday in volume of 26,200 shares. Shares have toppled from around 500 cents last September.
The Don Group on Thursday issued a cautionary announcement, following earlier one's this month, that it was still in talks. It gave no further details.
"Shares often move on the back of a cautionary," another dealer said.
